Rank 4 REFUTED in part: the claim that no test expects exit 2 is false, because check-comment-hygiene.test.sh:74 asserts skip_exit -eq 2 for a skipped .txt input. The surviving gap is narrower: the quality workflow still demands only zero violations (SKILL.md:135), so a run in which every file was skipped satisfies the stated gate.

New hazard the first pass missed: check-comment-hygiene.sh is a Python program (line 1 shebang #!/usr/bin/env python3) behind a .sh name, and the skill text names only the path. Invoked as bash scripts/check-comment-hygiene.sh <file>, bash parses the Python body and fails at line 21 with a shell syntax error, exiting 2 — the same code that means all files were skipped, so the two states are indistinguishable to a caller.

Rank 5 CONFIRMED but under-stated: every named enforcement-layer path exists (claude-posttooluse.cjs, git-hooks/pre-commit, install-git-hooks.sh, comment-hygiene.yml, dist-freshness.cjs), yet git config --get core.hooksPath resolves to /Users/michelkerkmeester/.config/git/hooks, not the repository's .skilled/scripts/git-hooks. File existence therefore does not prove the pre-commit layer is installed, and the probe rank 5 proposes must also read the host wiring.

Cross-rank coupling: the only executable checker quality owns skips YAML entirely — python3 check-comment-hygiene.sh on a tracked .github/workflows/comment-hygiene.yml returned exit 2 with no output — so rank 3's new .github/workflows routing must land together with rank 4's skipped-not-clean reporting, or the added routing manufactures false passes on the exact surface it adds.

INFERRED: the write-time warning is wired for Claude only — .claude/settings.json:227 runs the post-edit-quality adapter under PostToolUse — so a run under any other host receives no warning, which is rank 5's absent-layer problem one level above file existence.
